review_title: Very rigid refund policy despite limited usage and product complexity
review_text:
I purchased the Notion Business annual plan on January 14 for $288. After buying it, I spent time trying to integrate Notion into my workflow, but unfortunately I realized that the platform was not the right fit for my needs.

One of the biggest issues for me was how complex the system is for relatively simple use cases. Even basic workflow setups require a lot of manual configuration, and building structured processes takes significantly more time than expected.

In addition, some workflow and automation capabilities that I expected from a Business plan were either missing or required complicated workarounds. Because of this, I could not integrate Notion efficiently into my daily work.

When I contacted support, they explained their 30-day refund policy. I understand that policies exist, but when I requested support it had been less than two months since the purchase and my actual usage was quite limited.

They asked me to downgrade my workspace to the Free plan, which I did, but even after following their instructions they refused to offer any partial refund or credit for the unused months of the annual subscription.

I was not asking for a full refund anymore — only a reasonable prorated refund for the unused portion of the subscription.

It’s disappointing to see such a rigid approach, especially for small business users where $288 is a significant expense.

I hope Notion will reconsider situations like this in the future and provide more flexible solutions for customers who clearly did not fully use the service.

review_title: Deceptive Billing, Terrible Support, and Zero Accountability – Avoid Notion!
review_text:
I’m writing this review to warn others about Notion’s deceptive billing practices, inaccessible customer service, and complete lack of accountability. What started as a simple subscription downgrade request turned into a months-long nightmare that left me financially strained and deeply frustrated. If you’re considering Notion, think twice—their app might be sleek, but their customer service is a disaster.
Here’s what happened: I signed up for Notion’s premium plan but quickly realized the app didn’t offer the features I needed. I hadn’t used it in over two months, so on March 13, 2025, I emailed their support team to downgrade my account to the free plan, as their emails had stated I’d lose premium access if payment failed. I was fine with that—I just wanted out of the subscription. Instead of honoring my request, Notion kept trying to charge me. On March 18, 2025, the second funds hit my account, they deducted the payment—despite my clear instructions to downgrade.
I immediately requested a refund, explaining that I’m unemployed and needed the money for a specialist medical appointment that day. Because of Notion’s actions, I had to borrow money from my son to cover the cost, adding stress to an already difficult situation. Their response? A canned email from “the representative” (who, by the way, is just a Campus Ambassador, not even a proper support rep—more on that later), citing a 3-day refund window and refusing to help. The invoice they charged me for was issued on February 22, 2025, but I’d already requested a downgrade on March 13, well before the payment was taken. They ignored that completely.
